title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 733-735). U_1 = P^1 - {0,1,inf} over Q. U_n is the Fermat cover, the affine Fermat curve x^n + y^n = 1 minus the points above 0, 1 and infinity. Geometrically it is the maximal abelian exponent-n Galois cover of U_1, with group (Z/n)^2 = mu_n^2. Sequence (371) is the fundamental exact sequence 1 -> pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}) -> pi_1(U_n) -> Gamma_Q -> 1.

On the previous page Grothendieck argues as follows. Under the section conjecture, Fermat's theorem for U_n is equivalent to the claim that every splitting of (371) comes from a 'point at infinity' (a cusp). Proving that no non-cuspidal splittings exist would prove Fermat for U_n even without the full anabelian yoga. He proposes to get at this through successively finer 'Lie approximations' of M_{0,3}, i.e. of the arithmetic fundamental group of U_1 together with its symmetries.

This page:
(i) Any useful approximation must be at least as fine as the one developed in the present section. That one is the 'minimal' approximation in which the Fermat tower can be expressed 'algebraically' starting from M_{0,3} ⊂ M_{0,3}^et (cf. 13°).
(ii) Use the S_3 symmetry. S_3 permutes 0, 1, inf; equivalently it permutes the projective coordinates of X^n + Y^n + Z^n = 0. This action is defined over Q and preserves the cusps. So one can pass to the quotient stack [U_n/S_3]. Its fundamental group pi_1(U_n, S_3) sits in the richer sequence (372): 1 -> pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}) -> pi_1(U_n, S_3) -> Gamma_Q x S_3 -> 1. For n = 1 this group is pi_1(U_1, S_3) = M_{0,3}, the S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group of the tripod. The splittings of (371) are among the data carried by (372). Grothendieck expects this S_3-enriched extension to play an important role.
(iii) To match the Lie approximation of this section, (372) is replaced by a coarser quotient extension. One divides by a normal subgroup contained in pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}), namely pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}) ∩ [pihat_{0,3}, pihat_{0,3}]. This subgroup is normal because the commutator subgroup is characteristic in pihat_{0,3}, which is normal in M_{0,3}.

The next page gives the result, diagram (373). The kernel becomes Mhat[n] = pi_1(U_{n,Qbar})/(pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}) ∩ [pihat, pihat]). This is the image of the Fermat subgroup in pihat^ab = Mhat ≅ Zhat(1)^2, which is n·Mhat ≅ Mhat. The Galois action factors through the cyclotomic character chi. One obtains extensions of Zhat^* x S_3 by Mhat (groups written G~_{rho,sigma}[n]), all deduced 'algebraically' from the n = 1 extension (374). Those split as semidirect products, with canonical splittings coming from cusps / tangential base points.

The point of the passage is the following. The metabelian-level (H_1 of the base) approximation is the coarsest level at which the whole Fermat tower and its S_3 x Galois symmetry can be written down. Finer (nilpotent / Lie) approximations should then be used to test splittings of (371) and (372) as a route to Fermat's Last Theorem.
errors: No outright error. The constructions are correct: [pihat, pihat] is characteristic in pihat_{0,3}, so the quotient in (iii) is legitimate, and Mhat[n] maps isomorphically onto n·Mhat.

The quotient chosen in (iii) is far too coarse to say anything about Fermat. It discards H_1 of the Fermat curve itself (the Jacobian / Jacobi-sum part) and keeps only the image in pihat_{0,3}^ab. The quotient extensions always split, so this level carries no obstruction. Grothendieck implicitly acknowledges this by calling it the 'minimal' approximation and asking for finer ones.

The relation between (372) and Fermat is only heuristic. Splittings of (372) over Gamma_Q x S_3 are a stronger datum than splittings of (371). Non-existence of non-cuspidal S_3-equivariant splittings would not by itself exclude non-cuspidal splittings of (371).

ideas.what: Attack Fermat's Last Theorem through the section conjecture for the Fermat curves U_n: show every Galois section of pi_1(U_n) -> Gamma_Q is cuspidal.
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture for (affine) Fermat curves; Fermat via Galois sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (section conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); nilpotent / Ellenberg obstructions for Fermat curves by Ellenberg (c. 2000) and Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren (2010s)
ideas.where_published: The section conjecture and its link with Mordell are in the letter to Faltings. An explicit Fermat formulation is in these unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes; unsure whether it appears elsewhere.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group of the Fermat curve: the extension (372) of Gamma_Q x S_3 by pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}), with M_{0,3} = pi_1(U_1, S_3) as the case n = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of the quotient stack [U_n/S_3]; orbifold/equivariant fundamental exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard stacky formalism; Grothendieck's own 'multiplicités modulaires' viewpoint
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (S_3-symmetries of M_{0,4})

ideas.what: Successive 'Lie approximations' of M_{0,3} (quotients by lower central or derived series terms) used to test splittings of the Fermat extension. The metabelian level is the minimal one expressing the Fermat tower algebraically.
ideas.modern_name: Nilpotent / metabelian approximations of the section conjecture; Ellenberg obstructions; Kim's nonabelian Chabauty
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (metabelian Galois representations via Fermat Jacobians, 1986); Ellenberg; M. Kim (2005+); Wickelgren

ideas.what: Quotient of (372) by pi_1(U_{n,Qbar}) ∩ [pihat, pihat], giving extensions of Zhat^* x S_3 by Mhat ≅ Zhat(1)^2 with Galois action through the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Image of the Fermat tower in the abelianization; cyclotomic level of the Galois action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara / Anderson for the finer level (H_1 of Fermat curves, Jacobi sums)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out a program: study splittings of the S_3-enriched extension (372) of Gamma_Q x S_3 for the Fermat curves, at successively finer Lie (nilpotent) approximations of M_{0,3}, as a route to FLT. He expects the S_3-equivariant structure to be important. Later work on Ellenberg obstructions and Galois action on Fermat-curve homology (Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren) works with pi_1(U_n) and does not, as far as I know, systematically exploit the S_3-equivariant extension over Gamma_Q x S_3.
missed.quote: la suite exacte (371) se plonge d'ailleurs dans une suite exacte plus riche (372) ... cette structure d'extension plus riche jouera un rôle important
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Equivariant (stacky) sections over Gamma_Q x S_3 impose extra constraints and could sharpen nilpotent obstructions for rational points on Fermat curves. It also anticipates the later program of Ellenberg and Wickelgren.

missed.claim: Explicit link between the anabelian section conjecture for the Fermat tower and Fermat's Last Theorem, pursued through Lie / nilpotent approximations of the tripod group. This prefigures Ellenberg's nilpotent section obstructions and Kim's unipotent approach applied to Fermat curves, but in an S_3-equivariant, tower-uniform ('algebraic in n') form.
missed.quote: approximations de Lie au moins aussi fines que celles du présent §, qui apparaît comme l'approximation "minima" dans laquelle on puisse exprimer "algébriquement" la tour des courbes de Fermat
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the idea of nilpotent section obstructions for Fermat curves. It also suggests treating all n uniformly through M_{0,3}, rather than curve by curve.

deep.surprise_reason: The page by itself is modest: it sets up an equivariant extension and a coarse metabelian quotient. Its context is an explicit unpublished plan to prove FLT through non-existence of non-cuspidal sections, checked against finer Lie approximations of M_{0,3} with S_3 symmetry. That anticipates the Ellenberg/Wickelgren line of work. It is a notable unpublished program, not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: Index is U_m on this page in the transcription, but the neighbouring pages use U_n; read U_n throughout.
The line 'pi_1(Û_1, S_3) = M_{0,3}' is a handwritten annotation written under (372). It identifies the case n = 1, i.e. pi_1(U_1, S_3) = M_{0,3}.
The word struck out after 'Fermat,' appears to be a short word (perhaps 'ainsi'); 'comme on l'a vu dans 13°)' is correct.
On the previous page, '[?]variations de Lie' should read 'approximations de Lie'.
